source.title: Understanding deep learning requires rethinking generalization
source.authors: Chiyuan Zhang; Samy Bengio; Moritz Hardt; B. Recht; O. Vinyals

record.file_problem: Full paper text supplied; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The study trains neural networks with SGD on CIFAR-10 data with randomized labels or inputs and reports training accuracy/loss, directly testing whether gradient training fits those datasets.
record.gate_note: Cited findings from other studies are not recorded as rows. Rows cover the paper's own CIFAR-10 and ImageNet experiments, including random labels, pixels, Gaussian inputs, regularization conditions, and the reported CIFAR-10 batch-normalization comparison. Training-time slowdown and test accuracy are not separate rows because they do not measure the claimed training-error outcome.
record.test_reason: The study directly measures CIFAR-10 training classification accuracy after SGD training on true, corrupted and random labels. It is an original source for V1, so V1 verdict labels are suppressed.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate: the tested architectures can memorize training data, including random labels, and optimization can remain empirically easy despite poor generalization. The authors also argue that conventional complexity measures and explicit regularization do not adequately explain generalization. Exact fitting has reported exceptions, including regularized AlexNet and random-label ImageNet runs.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SGD with random initialization and reports classification training accuracy/loss on CIFAR10 and ImageNet; CIFAR-100 and Adam are not tested. The tested random-label, input-randomization and regularization conditions vary from the versions' broader scope.
record.method_sensitivity: Dataset, label corruption, input randomization, weight decay, data augmentation and model architecture/regularization alter the reported results; default weight decay prevents Alexnet convergence on random labels, while other tested models fit nearly or fully.

fits_no_version.finding: Fully connected MLPs attain high CIFAR-10 training accuracy, including on random labels; Table 1 reports 100% for MLP 3x512 and 99.34% for MLP 1x512 on random labels without weight decay.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SGD can fit random CIFAR-10 labels with fully connected ReLU networks.

fits_no_version.finding: Inception V3 reaches 87.81–95.20% top-1 training accuracy on random ImageNet labels across the reported regularization settings.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Large convolutional networks can fit most random ImageNet labels with asynchronous SGD, without necessarily attaining near-zero training error.

fits_no_version.finding: Convolutional networks fit independently permuted pixels and Gaussian input noise; Figure 1a presents Inception learning curves.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Convolutional networks can memorize training sets whose image structure has been destroyed.

fits_no_version.finding: Section 3.1 reports that batch normalization stabilizes Inception learning dynamics and improves generalization by about 3–4 percentage points.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Batch normalization can stabilize learning dynamics and improve generalization in CIFAR-10 Inception.

record.problems: No uncertainty estimates are reported for the extracted training results. The ImageNet random-label runs do not reach 100% top-1 training accuracy; the authors say they did no hyperparameter tuning when switching to random labels. Appendix E notes that augmented-sample training accuracy is an online average and the training set varies each epoch.
record.rows_left_out: No rows omitted under the 60-row limit. Figure-only training curves and test-accuracy outcomes were excluded because the cataloged claim concerns training classification error, and the relevant outcomes are available in text or tables.

untested.parts: CIFAR-100, Adam, smaller convolutional-model comparisons, and substantial training error caused by early stopping. Random initialization is not explicitly documented in the supplied experimental setup.
Teacher-student ReLU optimization, spurious local minima and extra student neurons.
Comparative initialization effects on training speed and trainable depth.
Learning rates relative to a measured stability threshold, curvature dynamics and recovery or divergence.

Faster accuracy gains, higher tolerated learning rates and Fixup comparisons. The supplied prose establishes stabilization from batch normalization, but does not establish a speed or learning-rate advantage.

missing.what: Inception with default weight decay attains 100% CIFAR-10 random-label training accuracy. R5 has weight decay disabled, and no other row records this convolutional-network regularization result.

record.verdict_notes: V1 labels are omitted because this study is an original source. None of the other versions has a sufficiently established matching result here. States marked cannot_determine for out-of-scope rows concern their applicability to the supplied versions, not uncertainty about correctly transcribed numerical results.

versions.untested_parts: CIFAR-100; Adam; smaller models, early stopping and recipes beyond those tested.
